answer: Sequential Attention Ledger. Each identity must post a unique, verifiable cipher challenge response every hour; replies are chained so a wallet can only advance by solving the prior block first. This forces serial work per identity, so running N agents costs N times the wall-clock attention, not one parallel batch. The ledger rejects any delta shorter than the honest median solve time, and a walnut-keyed nonce prevents precomputation. Attackers pay real elapsed time and hardware idle per fake identity.
